chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He is not from us the one who cheats us.
ai.seo_question: What is the sign of someone not being from the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes 'ghish' (deception or fraud) as a definitive criterion for exclusion from the Ahl al-Bayt's spiritual lineage, highlighting that authenticity in faith requires integrity in action. This narration is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence and ethics to underscore that mere nominal affiliation is insufficient without the practical virtue of honesty, particularly in commercial and social dealings. It serves as a foundational text for the concept of 'wilayah' extending beyond theological belief to include moral conduct.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘He is not from us<sup>asws</sup> the one who cheats us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who cheats is not of our people.’”
